paper.title: Gut bacteria and mood in mice

paper_text:
Gut bacteria and mood in mice
Lopez, D., Chen, W.  J. Fake Microbiology, 2022

Abstract
Transplanting gut bacteria from depressed donors made recipient mice less active in a forced-swim test (Figure 3).

Results
Figure 3 shows immobility time; Figure 4 shows bacterial counts.

alerts.description: An expression of concern was published for this paper.

notice.text:
Expression of concern: Gut bacteria and mood in mice

The editors have been made aware of concerns regarding some of the data reported in this article. The matter is being looked into and we will update readers when more information is available.

draft_text:
Microbiome and depression: a review

1. Discussion
The causal role of gut bacteria in depressive behaviour is supported by transplant studies, notably Lopez and Chen [8], who showed reduced activity in recipient mice. Our own proposal builds on this finding.

References
[8] Lopez, D., Chen, W. (2022). Gut bacteria and mood in mice. J. Fake Microbiology.

must_include: says the notice does not say which data or findings are in question
advises hedging the wording or not building new work on the finding
notes that the outcome of the investigation is not yet known
must_not_include: names a specific figure or table as the problem

expected.why: Expression of concern about data = medium (rubric). The notice names no part, so scope and 'affected' are unclear. Unclear counts as affected: key_evidence x medium = medium. Answering high would be overreach.
